clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 5393-7660 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8428.txt; 5 FR 2131, issue of Wednesday, June 5, 1940; the held text layer interleaves the page-1 contents list and the page-2 masthead between the order's opening words and its remaining sentences): signed June 3, 1940 under the authority of Executive Order No. 6166 of June 10, 1933. It revokes section 2 of Executive Order No. 6228 of July 28, 1933, which interpreted the order of June 10, 1933, only insofar as that section pertains to or affects the transfer of the Custer Battlefield National Cemetery in Montana, and provides that the order becomes effective on "July 1,1940". Its one command is a revocation, performed when it took effect; it imposes no continuing duty and has no term. First end: performance on the stated effective date, 1940-07-01. This is the order's own stated date; the exact moment of effect within that day is not stated. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 (evidence not convenience) the exhausted command is separated from its surviving consequence (see savings). No earlier end: before July 1, 1940 the order had not taken effect, and no held text suspends, postpones or revokes it.

I read the whole order; I did not inspect a page image (only the text layer is held). Whole-order status is no (provisional, already adopted). The order's only command is a partial revocation that took effect on its stated date July 1, 1940, where the command was exhausted by performance; the consequence survives as an accrued effect.

savings.reason: The revocation changed, from its effective date, the effect of section 2 of Executive Order No. 6228 on the transfer of the Custer Battlefield National Cemetery. That change persists independently of this order after the command was performed. Which agency administers the cemetery afterwards is not shown by the held order and is not decided here.
